## PDF page 9

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=9)

```text
                               CHAPTER TWO



                     EQUITY SETUPS


In poker, your equity is simply what percentage of the pot you are entitled to
based upon your chance of winning the hand at showdown. This is a number
from 0%-100%, where a higher number means you are entitled to more of the
pot and a lower number means you are entitled to less of the pot.

Equity is a key variable when it comes to completing expected value (EV) cal-
culations, and we will do plenty of those calculations later in this workbook.
For now, you will explore equity setups from a hand vs. hand, hand vs. range,
and range vs. range point of view.

Be sure to keep in mind that the equity number you arrive at is not a complete
picture of how good or bad a hand is. Factors like playability and postflop
edges are incredibly important when considering whether or not to get
involved with lower equity. But as stack sizes decrease and all-in situations
arise, knowing your hand vs. range equities will be your saving grace.

TOOLS TO USE: Flopzilla, Equilab, or PokerCruncher will work well.

PROCESS: Plug the hands and/or ranges into your software, calculate the
equity, and jot down everything for both players. Keep things tidy by rounding
your answers (40.42% equity rounds to 40%, and 76.81% equity rounds to 77%).
You can copy/paste the range strands (e.g., AA-88,AKs-ATs,AKo-AQo) into
```

```text
TAKEAWAYS: Understanding hand vs. hand will help you better estimate your
```
